{{Short description|American chemistry professor}}
'''Peter Wipf''' is a distinguished university professor of chemistry at the [[University of Pittsburgh]]. His research interests focus on the [[total synthesis]] of natural products, the discovery of new transformations of strained molecules, and the development of new pharmaceuticals.<ref name="Pharmacology"/><ref name="PittChem"/> He is a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] of Chemistry (RSC), the American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS), and the American Chemical Society (ACS).

==Education==
* Dipl. Chem., [[University of Zurich]], Switzerland, 1984<ref name="PittChem2">{{cite web |url=https://www.chem.pitt.edu/sites/default/files/person/wipf2_0.pdf |title=Peter Wipf, PhD Biographical Sketch |work=University of Pittsburgh Department of Chemistry website |publisher=[[University of Pittsburgh]] |accessdate=2017-03-10 }}</ref>
* Ph.D., [[University of Zurich]], Switzerland, 1987<ref name="PittChem2"/>
* Postdoctoral Fellow, [[University of Virginia]], USA, 1988-1990<ref name="PittChem2"/>

==Career==
Wipf joined the [[University of Pittsburgh]] Department of Chemistry in 1990, and has remained there ever since. He became a full professor in 1997, and a distinguished university professor of chemistry<ref name="PittProfs">{{cite web |url=http://www.provost.pitt.edu/faculty-affairs/distinguished.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070905185012/http://www.provost.pitt.edu/faculty-affairs/distinguished.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=2007-09-05 |title=Policy and Procedure Governing Appointments to Distinguished Professorships |work=University of Pittsburgh Faculty Handbook |publisher=[[University of Pittsburgh]] |date=2013-02-05 |accessdate=2017-03-16 }}</ref> in 2004. In 2001, he was appointed professor of pharmaceutical sciences in the School of Pharmacy. He is director of the university's Center for Chemical Methodologies & Library Development. He has been a visiting professor at the [[University of California, Irvine School of Physical Sciences|University of California, Irvine]], [[Paris-Sud University|Paris-Sud]], the [[ESPCI Paris|ESPCI]], and the [[University of Eastern Finland]].<ref name="PittChem2"/><ref name="c&en">{{cite web |url=http://cen.acs.org/articles/91/i29/Peter-Wipf-Wins-Morley-Medal.html?type=paidArticleContent |title=Peter Wipf Wins Morley Medal |work=Chemical & Engineering News |publisher=[[American Chemical Society]] |date=2013-07-22 |accessdate=2017-03-10 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170312060909/http://cen.acs.org/articles/91/i29/Peter-Wipf-Wins-Morley-Medal.html?type=paidArticleContent |archive-date=2017-03-12 |url-status=live }}</ref>

His research interests encompass synthetic organic and [[medicinal chemistry]], with a focus on natural products, the chemistry of strained molecules, and the discovery of new drugs.<ref name="Pharmacology">{{cite web |url=http://www.pharmacology.us/Faculty/PeterWipf?AspxAutoDetectCookieSupport=1 |title=Peter Wipf, PhD |work=University of Pittsburgh Department of Pharmacology and Chemical Biology website |publisher=[[University of Pittsburgh]] |accessdate=2017-03-10 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190202042937/http://www.pharmacology.us/Faculty/PeterWipf?AspxAutoDetectCookieSupport=1 |archive-date=2019-02-02 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="PittChem">{{cite web |url=http://www.chem.pitt.edu/person/peter-wipf |title=Peter Wipf / Department of Chemistry |work=University of Pittsburgh Department of Chemistry website |publisher=[[University of Pittsburgh]] |accessdate=2017-03-10 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170312061429/http://www.chem.pitt.edu/person/peter-wipf |archive-date=2017-03-12 |url-status=live }}</ref> He serves on many advisory and editorial boards in the fields of chemistry and pharmaceuticals.

==Publications==
Wipf is the author or coauthor of over 600 academic publications and a named inventor on more than 50 granted patents.<ref name="PubMed">{{cite web |url=https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed?cmd=Search&db=PubMed&term=%22Wipf+P%22%5Bau%5D+ |title="Wipf P"[au] |work=PubMed.gov |publisher=US National Library of Medicine, National Institutes of Health |accessdate=2017-03-10 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170314142836/https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed?cmd=Search&db=PubMed&term=%22Wipf+P%22%5Bau%5D+ |archive-date=2017-03-14 |url-status=live }}</ref> One hundred of his original research publications have been cited over 100 times in the literature, including:<ref name="PittChem2"/>

* {{cite journal | last1=Wipf | first1=Peter | last2=Lim | first2=Sungtaek | title=Total Synthesis of the Enantiomer of the Antiviral Marine Natural Product Hennoxazole A | journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society | publisher=American Chemical Society (ACS) | volume=117 | issue=1 | year=1995 | issn=0002-7863 | doi=10.1021/ja00106a075 | pages=558–559| bibcode=1995JAChS.117..558W }}

==Honors and awards==
Among many other honors and awards, Dr. Wipf is a:
* Recipient of the [https://www.acs.org/funding/awards/acs-award-for-creative-work-in-synthetic-organic-chemistry.html ACS Award for Creative Work in Synthetic Organic Chemistry] (2023)
* Recipient of the [[Humboldt Research Award]] of the [[Alexander von Humboldt Foundation]] (2014)
* Fellow of the [[American Chemical Society]] (2010)
* Recipient of the [[Ernest Guenther Award]] in the Chemistry of [[Natural product|Natural Products]] (2009)
* Fellow of the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]] (FRSC) (2004)
* Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] (2002)
* Recipient of the [https://www.acs.org/funding/awards/arthur-cope-scholar-award/past-recipients.html ACS Cope Scholar Award] (1998)
